issue_context.title: Worker code is not bundled when using the `new URL()` pattern
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Let’s say you want to run a worker with the following code:

```js
// worker.js
import constant from './module.js';

postMessage(constant);
```

The platform-y approach is to use the `new URL()` pattern, which is supported by vite:

```js
const w = new Worker(
  new URL('./worker.js', import.meta.url), 
  { type: 'module' }
);
```

However, with the `new URL()` pattern, the worker source is shipped _as is_, that is with no bundling of the dependency graph.

Using the `?worker` syntax, it works as expected.

```js
import myWorker from './worker.js?worker';
const w = new myWorker();
```

### Reproduction

[Repro](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-7s8grz?file=worker.js&terminal=dev) on StackBlitz.

### System Info

```shell
Stackbltiz.
```


### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

```shell
~/projects/vitejs-vite-7s8grz
❯ npm run build
$ vite build
vite v2.6.14 building for production...
✓ 3 modules transformed.
dist/assets/worker.a8662a62.js   0.06 KiB
dist/index.html                  0.11 KiB
dist/assets/index.52bcbe30.js    0.86 KiB / gzip: 0.50 KiB

~/projects/vitejs-vite-7s8grz
❯ cat dist/assets/worker.a8662a62.js
import constant from './module.js';

postMessage(constant);
```
```
